recipes.name: Crab-Stuffed Lobster Tail
ingredients_raw: 2 lobster tails, split along the center top
0.25 cup clarified butter, at room temperature
1 teaspoon seafood seasoning (such as Old Bay®)
0.25 teaspoon freshly ground white pepper, or to taste

steps.text: Gather the ingredients and preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
Pull the edges of the split lobster shells apart and gently lift tail meat to rest above the shells. Place tails onto a baking sheet and brush meat with melted butter.
Gently mix crabmeat, clarified butter, crushed crackers, parsley, lemon juice, seafood seasoning, lemon zest, garlic, salt, and pepper together in a bowl until thoroughly combined.
Spoon 1/2 of the mixture into each tail; press gently to pack mixture so it doesn’t fall off.

Bake in the preheated oven until meat is opaque and the stuffing is golden brown on top, 10 to 12 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the lobster tail should read 145 degrees F (65 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Crab-Stuffed Lobster Tail
raw_recipe.description: Enjoy stuffed lobster tails at home filled with a buttery cracker and crab stuffing instead of waiting for a night out at your local seafood restaurant.

review.reviewBody: This was a collaborative effort between Hubs and me. As this recipe's first reviewer I wanted to make sure I stuck to the recipe as closely as possible. For the most part I did, however, I did use a smidge less Old Bay and lemon zest, and omitted the garlic since I used 2 T. of crushed, buttery garlic croutons in place of the "buttery round (i.e., Ritz) crackers. For color interest, texture and extra flavor I added a couple tablespoons of finely chopped sweet red bell pepper. I didn't measure the lemon juice, just gave it a good squeeze. I found it needed NO salt. This tinkering is only a reflection of personal taste, and not a criticism of the recipe which I'm sure is find as it stands. I do have a criticism, however, and that is that the size of the lobster tail is not indicated, which could greatly affect the cooking time! We used four (6 oz.) tails, and Hubs baked them for 15 minutes! Any larger tail would have required longer cooking time - this recipe directs 10-12 minutes, but for what sized tail? Very good recipe overall. Hubs particularly enjoyed it, while I will always be a fan of strictly broiled lobster tail with hot drawn butter.

So my husband and I are picky eaters, and he does not eat but three vegetables, period. Therefore, I omitted the parsley and for fear of being too lemony, the lemon zest. Otherwise, I used all the ingredients as suggested. The only thing that kept me from giving this a five is that the thickest part of the lobster tail was undercooked. My suggestion is to bake the tail 2 1/2-3 minutes, remove from oven and stuff, and then bake for the time suggested. I would also suggest a jelly roll pan versus a cookie sheet, as I had to wipe out the excess butter from the bottom of my oven that melted during baking.

It was good, but the Old Bay overpowered the taste of the whole dish and made it a little too salty. Next time I make it, I think I will cut back on the Old Bay a little. I also used bread crumbs that I lightly toasted with butter in the oven instead of the butter crackers.

I made 5 (5oz) tails, and increased everything accordingly. Even though I piled the stuffing high, we had about a cup left over. Totally fine by me! It's amazing heaped on bread and toasted, which was the next day's indulgent breakfast. Possibly beacuse of how much stuffing I used, it took about 15 minutes for the tails to completely reach 145 degrees. By this time the crab was a little crusty on top, and we loved it. It wasn't burnt at all - just gave a nice counterpoint to the tender tail meat. If you have never used this technique to lay the tail meat on top, don't be scared off by it. It isn't terribly difficult. The meat will stick a little to the shell on top. I find it easiest to loosen the meat from the bottom first and then wiggle my finger slowly around until it's free. Any meat still clinging to the shell is easy to get after cooking.

First, to the reviewer saying it's much better with the mustard mayo mix... That doesn't necessarily make it better; just different. You never said whether or not you tried it both ways. I found this to be very good and a very simple recipe to present an elegant looking dish. I used already cooked tails. I baked the stuffing for a short time, then topped the tails with the stuffing and broiled them for a few minutes. I did cut back a bit on the zest. I served them with petite filet mignons and asparagus.

I will make it again but will cook the lobster tails a little first before adding the crab meat mix. The crab meat mix cooks faster than the inside meaty portion of the lobster tail. I think the crab meat mix creates a buffer that slows down the cooking process in the lobster.

I used the crab topping on filets we made on the grill. The only substitution I had to make was using regular butter for clarified. The final product was delicious, and everyone LOVED it. We will be using this recipe again. Thanks for sharing it!

I used the stuffing recipe for portabella mushrooms and it was excellent. The only changes I made was to add a little extra lemon juice and used canned crab (that's what I had) . I will definitely make this again but will omit the salt and use lump crab like the recipe calls for. My husband LOVED this and asked that I make it again as an entree with a vegetable!

This recipe was easy and my husband and I both enjoyed it. The only suggestion would be the size of the lobster tails. I got mine at Sam’s club and they were huge. Had to cook them longer than the 12 minutes. Getting the lobster meat to sit on top of the tail was the hardest part. (Probably because I had t done it before). Other than that the rest was easy and it tasted great. Will definitely be making this again.
I had three 4 oz. tails, and used a small cann of crab meat as well as some imitation crab, so we had lots of stuffing on top, but I think it all came out great and will make again!

the best thing I've ever tasted. Goes great with the Daily Gourmet copycat shrimp scamp
Similar to my recipe, but, I use shrimp in the stuffing. Can’t wait to try the crab, though! The Ritz crackers are a must.
Delish!!! I also added a little shrimp to the crab meat stuffing.
Stuck to recipe and came out great for our NYE romantic dinner! Larger tails need just a minute more. Will definitely make again!
So much easier than I thought. Husband loved it!!!!!!
Be careful with the salt and Old Bay. Mine ended up being too salty going by the recipe.
Very easy recipe and tasty. We had it for Christmas dinner and it was well enjoyed. It's a 'keeper' recipe!
I made it without the old Bay it came out excellent thanks for the ideas
I made this for my husband's birthday and it certainly was a "wow!" Thanks for the recipe!
